subsections.title: Overview
subsections.summary: What it is and why it matters.

blocks.html: Surveillance is watching people at scale — by governments, police, employers or companies. It includes cameras and facial recognition, licence-plate readers, phone location tracking, and the mass collection of internet traffic. Knowing what is being collected, and where, helps you decide when to take extra care — for example at a protest or crossing a border.

subsections.title: Terminology
subsections.summary: The words you will run into.

items.title: Mass surveillance
items.html: Collecting data on everyone rather than on a specific suspect.

items.title: Facial recognition
items.html: Software that identifies people from camera images or photos.

items.title: ALPR
items.html: Automated licence-plate readers that log where cars go.

items.title: Geofence warrant
items.html: A request for every device that was in a certain place at a certain time.

items.title: Threat model
items.html: Working out who you are protecting yourself from, and what they can do, so you can choose the right protections.
